CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions and fatigue.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Eugene Walker is a 61-year-old male presenting for routine follow-up. He reports increased fatigue, which he attributes to either age or end-of-day exhaustion. He continues to ride his road bike 20-30 miles at a time, though he notes he is slower than previously and requires rest after long rides. He previously could ride 40 miles on a good day. He states his friend Tyler, who is older, now waits for him during rides. The patient is concerned about his aortic valve replacement, which was performed on 1/22/2013, as he is now eight years post-surgery and was told the valve would last approximately eight years. He requested an echocardiogram to assess valve function. His last stress test was on 9/9/2019. He denies any drastic changes since last visit. He no longer follows up at Hopkins due to stress. He reports pursed lip breathing when walking, as noted by his wife and other doctors, but denies associated wheezing. He also reports a small nodule on his right epididymis that he is not overly concerned about but wanted evaluated. He denies depression and describes himself as a happy person overall. Sleep varies from six to seven hours per night. He gets out of bed by 7:00 AM for work and lectures, attempts morning workouts, and swims twice weekly at 5:45 AM. He reports snoring but wife has not mentioned apnea episodes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No wheezing associated with pursed lip breathing. Denies depression. No other systems reviewed documented.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013.

MEDICATIONS
Vitamin D3: 50,000 units on Sundays, 2,000 units on other six days.
Clindamycin prior to dental procedures.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works in academic setting, lectures. Exercises regularly including road biking 20-30 miles and swimming twice weekly at 5:45 AM. Attempts morning workouts. Married. Does not follow up at Hopkins.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Overall doing well. Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing noted, low exhalation phase, clear to auscultation, no wheezing. Genitalia: Right testicle with two to three millimeters palpable nodule on epididymis, does not appear to be varicocele; left testicle normal; no hernia. All other portions of physical exam normal.

RESULTS
Recent blood work from 4/10/2021: Alkaline phosphatase elevated at 156. Lipid panel: total cholesterol 247, HDL 66, LDL 166, triglycerides 74. TSH normal at 2.68. CBC unremarkable. Vitamin D level at high end of normal at 94.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
History of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair: Patient is eight years post-op and asymptomatic. Will obtain echocardiogram and stress test. Referral to cardiology, recommended physician Dr. Vincent Sanchez.

Elevated alkaline phosphatase at 156: Likely related to bone health rather than liver. Will recheck alkaline phosphatase and GGT today.

Pursed lip breathing with low exhalation phase: Patient reports increased fatigue with biking though able to maintain 20-30 miles. Will order pulmonary function tests for further evaluation.

Right testicular nodule: Two to three millimeters palpable on right epididymis. Referral to urology for ultrasound evaluation.

Preventive health: MMR vaccine to be administered today. Shingles vaccine recommended, to be scheduled for next month. COVID-19 vaccination series completed (first dose 1/15/2021, second dose 2/5/2021).

Follow-up: Return in one year for wellness visit, sooner if needed based on results of pending labs and studies. Patient to call with any questions or concerns.
